description: The complete solar day for one location: sunrise, sunset, solar noon, day length, civil, nautical and astronomical twilight boundaries, and explicit polar day/night status at high latitudes. Location required. For a series, send start and end (step is whole days, e.g. "1d" or "7d"). For "is it dark enough to observe" prefer astro_dark_window; for a broad snapshot prefer astro_sky_today.

cursor.description: Opaque pagination cursor from a previous result's next_cursor. Send it with the same start/end arguments as the first page.

date.description: Single day to report, ISO 8601 UTC date or datetime, e.g. "2026-08-06" or "2026-08-06T21:00:00Z". Or jd: followed by a Julian Day on the UT scale, e.g. "jd:2461000.5". On astro_positions, date may list up to 24 datetimes separated by commas, answered in the order sent. Omit for the current moment. Years 1700 to 2200 only; outside that range the API refuses with DATE_OUT_OF_RANGE because the ephemeris is not reliable there.

end.description: Last day of a range. ISO 8601 UTC date or datetime, e.g. "2026-08-06" or "2026-08-06T21:00:00Z". Or jd: followed by a Julian Day on the UT scale, e.g. "jd:2461000.5". On astro_positions, date may list up to 24 datetimes separated by commas, answered in the order sent. Omit for the current moment. Years 1700 to 2200 only; outside that range the API refuses with DATE_OUT_OF_RANGE because the ephemeris is not reliable there.

lat.description: Latitude in decimal degrees, north positive. Send lat and lon together.

lon.description: Longitude in decimal degrees, east positive (Lisbon is about -9.14). Send lat and lon together.

place.description: Place name instead of lat/lon, as "City" or "City,CC" with an ISO country code, e.g. "Lisbon,PT". Resolved server-side; the response then carries a required GeoNames CC BY 4.0 credit in its attribution field, which must be preserved when shown.

start.description: First day of a range (use with end instead of date). ISO 8601 UTC date or datetime, e.g. "2026-08-06" or "2026-08-06T21:00:00Z". Or jd: followed by a Julian Day on the UT scale, e.g. "jd:2461000.5". On astro_positions, date may list up to 24 datetimes separated by commas, answered in the order sent. Omit for the current moment. Years 1700 to 2200 only; outside that range the API refuses with DATE_OUT_OF_RANGE because the ephemeris is not reliable there.

step.description: Range stride in whole days, e.g. "1d", "7d", "30d". Default "1d".

tz.description: IANA timezone like "Europe/Lisbon" to render event times in local time. Optional; a resolved place supplies its own timezone.

name: astro_sun

outputSchema.description: The MCP projection of a CycleCalcs v2 response: the answer, plus the provenance a caller needs to use it honestly.

attribution.description: The credit line to display verbatim when rights is attribution_required.

data.description: The complete solar day for one location, or one row per day in range mode.

blue_hour.description: The blue-light window just outside golden hour.

constellation.description: The IAU constellation the Sun currently occupies.

custom.description: Boundaries for any custom depression angles requested.

day_length_change_from_yesterday_seconds.description: Seconds gained or lost since the previous day. Negative means shortening.

days.description: RANGE MODE ONLY: one entry per day, each with the fields above.

golden_hour.description: The warm-light window around sunrise and sunset.

night_begins.description: When astronomical night starts. Null where it never gets that dark.

night_ends.description: When astronomical night ends. Null where it never gets that dark.

position_now.description: Where the Sun is at this moment.

rise_set.description: Sunrise and sunset, with a status for polar day and polar night.

solar_midnight.description: Instant the Sun is lowest, opposite solar noon.

solar_midnight_altitude_deg.description: Sun altitude at solar midnight, in degrees.

solar_noon.description: Instant the Sun crosses the meridian.

solar_noon_altitude_deg.description: Sun altitude at solar noon, in degrees.

solar_noon_azimuth_deg.description: Compass bearing of the Sun at solar noon.

summary.description: A one-line reading of the solar day.

tropical_sign.description: Tropical ecliptic longitude, reported as position only.

twilight.description: Civil, nautical and astronomical twilight boundaries.

window.description: The instant or range actually evaluated, after parsing.

next_cursor.description: Present only when more rows exist. Send it back with the SAME start/end arguments as the first call to get the next page.

not_computed.description: Data this API deliberately does not serve, and why. Present only when the question touched such a field. An absence named here is information: treat it as "withheld", never as "none exists".

rights.description: Either unrestricted, or attribution_required when third-party place data was used. When attribution_required, the attribution line must be shown.

warnings.description: Machine-readable notices about this answer. Present only when non-empty. Never changes whether the call succeeded.

title: Sunrise, sunset and twilight
